newsitem.title: USA: BPA bid to lift power line capacity goes to WSCC.
newsitem.headline: BPA bid to lift power line capacity goes to WSCC.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Thursday its plan to partially lift capacity restrictions on Pacific Intertie will go to the board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) on Friday.
Final approval of the plan, however, is expected to take at least 30 more days since the 77 member representatives of the regional reliability council also have to review it.

The Intertie lines, which run from the Pacific Northwest to California, have a rated capacity of 7,900 megawatts (MW), but have been restricted to 5,200 MW since last August after two power blackouts hit several western states.
Based on voltage support improvements, BPA had proposed raising the capacity to 6,500 MW by March, but a WSCC study group approved a rise only to 6,250 MW.
BPA would like to have the interstate transmission capacity increased in time for the spring runoff, when hydropower output hits an annual peak and regional power demand shifts toward the Southwest.
A BPA spokeswoman said the agency is hopeful that a further increase of the line capacity will win initial study group approval in early March, after which it would also enter a 30-day review period.
